newsitem.title: USA: CME LIVE CATTLE SEEN STEADY TO DOWN, FEEDERS MIXED.
newsitem.headline: CME LIVE CATTLE SEEN STEADY TO DOWN, FEEDERS MIXED.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower while calls on feeder cattle ranged from 0.100 cent higher to 0.100 lower, livestock analysts said.
Although live cattle futures were technically strong after last week's late rally, analysts expect early pressure on an overbought condition and weak daily fundamentals.
Boxed beef values continued to slip late last week and cash cattle prices were seen slipping further on reduced packer bids, analysts said.
However, the possibility of retailer interest in booking beef for Labor Day features could limit losses, they added. Labor Day this year will be observed on September 7.
Choice boxed beef values fell at total of $5.20 to $5.61 per cwt last week, according to USDA figures.
Feeder cattle futures may show little direction and could be influenced by either live cattle or corn futures.
Expectations of a sharp break in corn futures Monday morning may prompt support and offset effects of a recent drop in cash feeder cattle prices, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.48 at $81.53 per cwt.
